s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of systemic illness with fever, respiratory symptoms, and skin lesions
salient_findings: Multifocal alveolar infiltrates on chest radiography and CT
key_facts: 43-year-old man with no significant medical history
4-day history of fever, shaking chills, hemoptysis, and worsening dyspnea
Several months of intermittent night sweats, arthralgias, and 10-kg weight loss
Painful ecchymotic lesion on left calf with similar lesions on abdomen, back, and arms
Recent respiratory illness in 3-year-old son
Temperature 35.3 °C, blood pressure 117/75 mmHg, pulse 112 beats/min, respiratory rate 29 breaths/min
Oxygen saturation 96% on room air
Bilateral wheezes and multiple painful ecchymoses with hemorrhagic bullae
WBC count 9000/mm3, hemoglobin 13.4 g/dL, normal renal and liver function
Elevated lactate dehydrogenase, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, and C-reactive protein
Negative tests for cryoglobulin, protein C, protein S, rheumatoid factor, and anti–cyclic citrullinated peptide antibodies
Positive antinuclear antibody titer, lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin IgM, and anti–phosphatidylserine IgM
FilmArray respiratory panel positive for respiratory syncytial virus

shortlist.label: Antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Positive antinuclear antibody titer, lupus anticoagulant, and presence of skin lesions

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis
shortlist.why_kept: Respiratory symptoms, skin lesions, and elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate

shortlist.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of hemoptysis, dyspnea, and skin lesions

shortlist.label: Microscopic polyangiitis
shortlist.why_kept: Renal and pulmonary involvement, and presence of skin lesions

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including fever, hemoptysis, and worsening dyspnea, along with the presence of painful ecchymotic lesions and hemorrhagic bullae, are consistent with a vasculitic process. The positive antinuclear antibody titer, lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin IgM, and anti–phosphatidylserine IgM also suggest an autoimmune component. Although the tests for antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies were negative, the clinical presentation and the presence of superficial and deep dermal thrombotic paucicellular vasculopathy involving skin appendages are more consistent with antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis than the other options.

rejected.label: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis
rejected.why: The patient's presentation lacks the characteristic eosinophilia and asthma associated with this condition.

rejected.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
rejected.why: The patient's presentation lacks the characteristic granulomatous inflammation and upper respiratory tract involvement associated with this condition.

rejected.label: Henoch-Schönlein purpura
rejected.why: The patient's age and the presence of hemoptysis and worsening dyspnea are not typical for this condition, which is more commonly seen in children and presents with palpable purpura, abdominal pain, and arthritis.

rejected.label: Microscopic polyangiitis
rejected.why: The patient's presentation lacks the characteristic renal involvement and the presence of perinuclear antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies associated with this condition.
